statement: Three equal squares make an L shape: two squares side by side, and one more square on top of the left one. How many lines of symmetry does the L shape have?

choices.misconception: I only tried lines going straight up and down or straight across, and none of those work.
I thought the two lines of the rectangle made by the bottom squares still work for the L.
I thought each of the three squares adds one line of symmetry.
I counted the lines of symmetry of one square and forgot the rest of the shape.

hints: Do not only try lines that go straight up or straight across.
A line of symmetry can be slanted. Draw the L and try a fold through its corner square, from corner to corner, and check where the two arms land.
Fold along the slanted line through the corner square of the L. The arm going up lands on the arm going right.

solutions.reliable: Fold straight down or straight across and the halves do not match, because the L has one arm sticking up and one sticking out to the side. Now fold along the slanted line through the corner square, from its outer corner to its inner corner. The corner square folds onto itself and the two arms land on each other. No other line works, so the L has exactly 1 line of symmetry. The idea to keep: always check slanted lines too.

whyOnTest: Students look only for upright lines of symmetry, and this shape has a single slanted one, so it tests looking in every direction.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
